steps.announcement: Delete right leaf 5. Root 4's balance factor rises to 2, leaving it unbalanced.

steps.key_state: After 5 is deleted, root 4 has only left child 2, and 2 has left child 1 and right child 3. Four nodes remain, and the root's balance factor is 2.

steps.key_state: Deleting 5 and 3 leaves a leftward chain of 3 nodes: 4 → 2 → 1.

prose.summary: Repeatedly deleting nodes on one side of a binary search tree without rebalancing can make the subtree heights differ too much and reduce the tree to a one-sided chain.
prose.title: Deletions can turn a search tree into a chain
